tool.name: qpcrpredict
tool.description: trained positive/negative calls from raw real-time PCR run files (.eds, .rdml)
tool.command: ## the format is detected from the file content, the link only keeps a readable name in the report ln -s '$run' 'run_file' && qpcrpredict predict --run 'run_file' #if str($assay_source.source) == 'packaged' --target '$assay_source.target' #else --target '$assay_source.target_name' --assay '$assay_source.assay' #end if --model '$model' ## TabPFN models are licensed for non-commercial use and not for hosted services. They are refused ## unless the server operator has set QPCRPREDICT_ALLOW_TABPFN=1 in the job environment. \$( [ "\${QPCRPREDICT_ALLOW_TABPFN:-0}" = "1" ] || echo '--disallow-family tabpfn' ) #if str($sample).strip() != '' --sample '$sample' #end if --out '$predictions' --quiet

param.name: run
param.label: qPCR run file (.eds or .rdml)
param.help: One run file: an Applied Biosystems .eds project file, or an RDML file as exported by most qPCR software. The format is detected from the content.

param.name: source
param.label: Assay
param.help: The assay configuration defines the targets, the reference gene, the control names and the thresholds. Use the built-in AML MRD assay, or supply your own configuration (JSON, see 'qpcrpredict assay --show generic').
param.option: Built-in assay: AML molecular MRD (reference ABL1)

param.name: target
param.label: Target
param.help: The tool reads the replicate wells of this target and the reference wells of the same sample.

param.name: target_name
param.label: Target
param.help: A target name or alias of the assay, or the detector name as written on the plate.

param.name: model
param.label: Model bundle (.pkl)
param.help: A released model of the publication (aml_mrd.pkl with the laboratory thresholds, aml_mrd_abl10k.pkl with 10,000 ABL1 copies required for a negative call), downloaded from the data deposit and uploaded to the history, or a bundle trained with 'qpcrpredict train'. The tool ships no model. Model bundles are pickle files; only use bundles from a source you trust. Bundles of the TabPFN families are refused unless the server operator has enabled them, see the help below.

param.name: sample
param.label: Single sample (optional)
param.help: Leave empty to score every sample that carries the target in the run, or give one sample name.

tool.help:
**What it does**
``qpcrpredict`` is part of the LeukoPredict tools. It predicts the **positive** or **negative** call of a qPCR assay directly from the raw run file. Only the instrument data are used: the shape of the amplification curves and the Ct and quantity of the selected target and of the reference gene of the same sample. A quality and review gate turns runs that cannot be evaluated into an explicit **n.d.** (not evaluable, repeat) decision and borderline cases into a **review** flag for human classification.
The tool ships no model. The released models of the publication were trained for AML molecular measurable residual disease (mutated NPM1, RUNX1::RUNX1T1, CBFB::MYH11, PML::RARA and BCR::ABL1, normalised to ABL1) and are downloaded from the data deposit (see the documentation, https://qpcrpredict.readthedocs.io/en/latest/models/) and uploaded to the history as a dataset. For any other assay, supply your own assay configuration and a model trained with ``qpcrpredict train``.
**Inputs**
* *qPCR run file* - an Applied Biosystems ``.eds`` file or an RDML file. * *Assay* - the built-in AML MRD assay, or an assay configuration (JSON) from the history. * *Target* - the target to score. * *Model bundle* - a released model from the data deposit, or a bundle trained with ``qpcrpredict train``. * *Single sample* (optional) - restrict scoring to one sample.
**Output**
A tabular file with one row per sample: the ``decision`` (positive / negative / review / na) and its reported wording in ``call`` (n.d. for a run that cannot be evaluated), the call and probability of the model, the material quality, the key readouts (target Ct, reference copies, standard-curve R2, target/reference ratio) and the reason and recommendation for every deferred sample.
**TabPFN models need to be enabled by the server operator**
``qpcrpredict`` can train models of the TabPFN families on the command line. The pretrained TabPFN models are licensed by Prior Labs GmbH for non-commercial use only, and their license does not permit making them available as part of a hosted service without a commercial license. Whether this applies to a Galaxy server is a decision of its operator, who is the licensee of the TabPFN weights on that server. By default this tool therefore refuses model bundles of the TabPFN families. All other model families can be used.
An operator who is entitled to run TabPFN models, for example on an in-house server used for non-commercial research or with a commercial license, enables them by setting the environment variable ``QPCRPREDICT_ALLOW_TABPFN=1`` for this tool in the Galaxy job configuration::
<destination id="qpcrpredict_tabpfn" runner="local"> <env id="QPCRPREDICT_ALLOW_TABPFN">1</env> </destination>
**Note**
The output supports the decision and does not replace expert review of the amplification curves, in particular for low-level and borderline cases, which the tool flags as *review*.
